extra.message: Remote Code Execution via eval() in /evaluate — Full compromise of the server; attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands, exfiltrate data, or pivot internally. [verified: No input sanitization or authentication is applied to the 'expression' parameter before it is passed to eval() on line 120. An attacker can submit arbitrary Python code, e.g., __import__('os').popen('id').read(), achieving remote code execution.]

Hardcoded Flask Secret Key Enables Session Forgery — Privilege escalation, authentication bypass, access to authenticated endpoints. [verified: Line 15 hardcodes the Flask secret_key to a well-known string, allowing attackers to forge session cookies. No randomization or runtime override exists; the application uses this key to sign sessions, enabling authentication bypass.]

Plaintext Password Storage — Exposure of user credentials; attackers can reuse passwords across other services. [verified: User passwords are stored directly via self.password = password at line 30, with no hashing or encryption, as seen in lines 62-64 where request.form['password'] is assigned to the User model.]
